faqs.answer: OpenClaw is a framework you build on; GAIA is an assistant you use. If you want to configure automations in code, OpenClaw fits. If you want help today, GAIA does.
faqs.question: How is GAIA different from OpenClaw?

faqs.answer: GAIA offers a free tier, and Pro is a flat ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month. Self-hosted GAIA has no per-run metering.
faqs.question: How much does GAIA cost?

faqs.answer: Inventory the OpenClaw automations you actually rely on, connect the same tools to GAIA, and describe each workflow in plain words. GAIA rebuilds them without code.

name: OpenClaw
painPoints: Framework, not product: everything needs building first
Requires technical setup and ongoing maintenance
No proactive help until you configure it yourself
Connecting each tool means more custom work

whyPeopleLook: OpenClaw is genuinely impressive, and genuinely a second job. Users love the idea and tire of the upkeep: every integration is a project, every automation needs debugging, and the inbox still fills while you maintain scripts. People searching for an OpenClaw alternative want the same open-source automation energy with zero homework: connect tools, describe outcomes, done.
